spec_family.name: Exterior Entry Door Prime and Paint
spec_family.description: EA-based spec for new construction exterior entry doors. Three substrate materials (steel/fiberglass/wood) with substrate-driven primer selection. Complexity tier (single_slab/panel/grand_entry) is the primary cost driver. Hardware removal standard practice. Fiberglass = 100% acrylic only (oil prohibited). IR-reflective mandatory for LRV <30. Six-side sealing for wood doors. Door casing belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1.

includes: Door slab both faces (exterior and interior)
All 4 door edges (top, bottom, hinge, latch)
Glass lite masking (panel and grand_entry doors)
Substrate-driven primer application (DTM for steel, acrylic for fiberglass/wood, tannin spot for wood knots)
Two finish coats (standard or premium acrylic enamel, or IR-reflective for LRV < 30)
Six-side seal verification for wood doors

excludes.item: Door casing prep, prime, and paint

excludes.route_to: PROHIBITED — introduces orange peel on door faces
EXCLUDED — exterior entry doors are architectural focal points requiring minimum QT3

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling pace, scrutiny level, intercoat sanding, and defect tolerance.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3=standard (production pace, 6-foot visual, no intercoat sand). QT4=premium (slower pace, raking light at 3 feet, intercoat sand 220-grit). QT5=supreme (meticulous pace, arm's length lighted inspection, hand-sand 220/320, DFT verification, door may be removed for controlled environment painting). QT2 excluded — entry doors are high-visibility architectural focal points.

configuration_dimensions.description: Door substrate material — drives primer system, topcoat chemistry, and prep protocol.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Steel: DTM primer, solvent clean + degloss, no back-rolling. Fiberglass: 100% acrylic ONLY (oil prohibited), mild soap wash, light scuff on paint-grade only. Wood: acrylic primer, 120-150 grit sand, tannin spot prime knots, six-side seal mandatory. Per-door capture for mixed-substrate projects.

configuration_dimensions.description: Door complexity classification — PRIMARY cost driver. Routes to correct production rate tier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Single_slab: flat flush door, no glass, no panels — baseline 90-120 min. Panel: raised panel door with glass lites, recesses, caulk joints — 1.60x. Grand_entry: door slab + sidelites + transom, extensive glass masking, mullion painting, additional hardware — 3.50x. Per-door capture (project may have mixed complexity).
No locked-in default. Semi-gloss is most common for exterior doors. Steel doors: caution with gloss per ANSI A250.8 (emphasizes welding marks). Gloss requires higher prep quality.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for face coating.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray is primary for door faces (factory-smooth finish quality). Brush for panel recesses, all 4 edges, detail work, and small projects where spray setup is not justified. Roller is NOT valid — introduces orange peel on door faces. Back-rolling AVOIDED on metal doors.

paintable_items.name: Exterior entry door assembly
paintable_items.counting_rules: Each door assembly is 1 EA regardless of physical size. Grand entry with sidelites/transom is still 1 EA. Complexity and substrate dimensions determine rate per EA. A door assembly includes both faces, all 4 edges, frame/jamb, and glass lite painting (mullions).
paintable_items.notes: Single paintable item. Does NOT include casing (SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 scope). Complexity dimension (single_slab/panel/grand_entry) drives time per EA. Substrate material (steel/fiberglass/wood) drives primer system and prep protocol.

variants.notes: Standard spray on single slab door. No glass masking needed. Full hardware removal.
Standard spray on panel door. Includes glass masking, panel recess brush work.
Standard spray on grand entry. Extensive glass masking, mullion/sidelite/transom painting. 3.50x complexity modifier.
Premium spray on panel door. Intercoat sanding 220-grit. Premium acrylic enamel.
Supreme spray on grand entry. Door removed for controlled environment painting. Hand-sand 220/320-grit. DFT verification. Gravity leveling. Flagged for hourly pricing review (exceeds 4.0x cap).
Standard brush on single slab. May be faster than spray for single-door projects (no spray equipment setup).
Standard spray on factory-primed door. Skip prime module. Two finish coats only.
Standard spray on field-primed door. Skip prime module entirely. Two finish coats.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of exterior doors to paint. Each door assembly is 1 EA regardless of size.
Door complexity classification — single_slab, panel, or grand_entry. PRIMARY cost driver.
Door substrate material — steel, fiberglass, or wood. Drives primer system and prep protocol.
Boolean flag confirming new construction context. Always true for this NC spec.

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When door has glass lites (panel or grand_entry complexity)
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of exterior doors with glass lites requiring masking.
Count of hardware groups to remove/reinstall per door. Standard = 1 group per door. Grand entry may have 2+ groups.
Adjacent entry walkway/porch/stoop area requiring drop cloth protection.
Number of building elevations — used for per-elevation access type determination.
Access type per elevation. Doors are typically ground level. Ladder modifier only for elevated entries (deck/raised porch).

valid_input_states.notes: Four NC-relevant substrate states. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is dominant for steel/fiberglass. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is dominant for wood doors. SS_EXT_BARE_METAL is rare in NC (most steel doors arrive factory-primed). SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD for split-mobilization scenarios.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen. Semi-gloss is most common for exterior doors.

SS_EXT_BARE_METAL.notes: Bare steel requires DTM primer. CRITICAL: prime same day as surface prep — rust begins within hours.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Acrylic primer for bare wood and unprimed fiberglass. 100% acrylic MANDATORY for fiberglass. Wood: tannin spot prime knots with SYS_EXT_DOOR_PRIMER_TANNIN_SPOT before full coat.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Factory-primed steel/fiberglass may skip field prime if adhesion test passes. Light degloss/scuff still required.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD.notes: Field-primed surfaces skip prime module entirely. Direct to finish coats.

material_systems.name: DTM Primer for Steel Exterior Doors
material_systems.notes: Rust-inhibitive DTM primer for bare carbon steel doors. Prime SAME DAY as surface prep. Factory-primed steel with good adhesion skips this system.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Primer for Fiberglass and Wood Doors
material_systems.notes: MANDATORY for fiberglass — oil-based/alkyd primers PROHIBITED due to outgassing blister risk. For wood: general primer for non-tannin species; spot-prime knots separately with alkyd on tannin-rich species.

material_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots on Wood Doors
material_systems.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (mahogany, cedar, redwood, fir). Not a full-surface system. Applied by brush to individual knots before full acrylic primer coat.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Door Paint
material_systems.notes: Mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior enamel for QT3. Fiberglass doors: 100% acrylic ONLY. Replaced by SYS_EXT_DOOR_FINISH_IR_REFLECTIVE when color LRV < 30.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Door Paint
material_systems.notes: Premium acrylic enamel (SW Emerald, BM Aura Grand Entrance). Enhanced UV resistance, color retention, hardness. Replaced by SYS_EXT_DOOR_FINISH_IR_REFLECTIVE when color LRV < 30.

material_systems.name: IR-Reflective Exterior Door Paint for Dark Colors
material_systems.notes: MANDATORY for dark colors (LRV < 30). CICPs drop surface temperature 20-30 deg F. HARD STOP — without IR-reflective: wood warping, steel expansion, fiberglass outgassing.

production_summary.rate_basis: EA (each door assembly) — hours per door, not SF/hr or LF/hr

ea_conversion.notes: Standard entry door: ~20 SF per face x 2 faces + edges + frame. Single slab ~30-35 SF. Panel ~35-45 SF. Grand entry ~45-55 SF (includes sidelite/transom frames).

time_estimates_by_scenario.scenario: Single slab, steel, factory-primed, spray, QT3
time_estimates_by_scenario.notes: Minimum scope — no prime module, no glass masking, no intercoat sand.
Full scope with panel recess work, intercoat sand, glass masking. 1.60x complexity modifier.

time_estimates_by_scenario.scenario: Grand entry, wood, bare, spray, QT5
time_estimates_by_scenario.notes: Maximum scope. 3.50x complexity modifier. Flagged for hourly pricing review.

production_summary.worst_case_stack: Grand entry (3.50) x QT5 (1.30) x wood (1.10) x ladder (1.35) x environmental = ~10.21x theoretical, capped to 4.0x

protection_zones_required.notes: Glass lites in door slab and sidelites/transom. Tape edge seal + HDPE static-cling film. QT5: liquid mask for razor-sharp lines. This spec owns glass masking when painting the DOOR — distinct from trim spec which masks glass adjacent to CASING.
Hardware is REMOVED per doctrine — not masked. Areas beneath hardware must be sealed. Photograph layout before removal. Labeled bags. Standard door = 1 group. Grand entry may have 2+ groups.
Pull out friction-fit stripping or deep-tape non-removable stripping. NEVER paint weatherstripping — destroys elasticity. 1:1 with door count.
Tape and plastic over threshold to catch drips during edge and face painting. Critical during bottom edge painting. 1:1 with door count.
Entry walkway/porch/stoop. Canvas for crew traffic, plastic for spray overspray containment.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Door casing frames the door opening. Different color typically. SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 scope. Casing-to-wall caulking is trim spec responsibility.
Exterior door frame/jamb — IN scope of this spec. Same finish as door slab.
Siding-to-door junction: no direct adjacency — casing intervenes. No deduplication needed.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: All labor tasks at elevation (does NOT apply to ground-level protection or FIXED per-project tasks)
site_condition_rules.notes: Most exterior doors are at grade. Ladder modifier for elevated deck/raised porch entries. Scaffold/lift rarely applicable.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: Spray application tasks and masking tasks
site_condition_rules.notes: High wind excludes spray tasks entirely — flag for re-scope. Moderate wind adds 25% overhead.
Full sun compresses working window (flash dry, blistering risk on dark colors). Especially critical for dark door colors on steel substrate.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: All prime and finish coat application tasks
site_condition_rules.notes: Cold (< 50F) slows cure, risks adhesion. Hot (> 85F) causes flash dry and streaking. Critical for dark colors on steel (thermal mass).

adjacent_specs.relationship: Door casing painting belongs to trim spec. Glass masking ownership: door spec masks glass when painting the DOOR; trim spec masks glass adjacent to CASING. Casing-to-wall caulking is trim spec scope.

cross_spec_boundaries.cross_spec_protection_note: Siding-to-door junction: no direct adjacency — casing intervenes. No deduplication needed.
deduplication_notes: Door CASING painting belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 — this spec covers door slab, edges, frame/jamb, and glass lite masking only.
Glass masking ownership: when painting the DOOR, this spec masks the glass. When painting the CASING, the trim spec masks adjacent glass (ext_door_glass_adjacent zone).
Door-to-frame weatherseal gap is PROTECTED (not caulked) by this spec. Casing-to-wall caulking is trim spec scope.

round_configurations.description: 1 prime coat + 2 finish coats — standard NC sequence for bare substrates
2 finish coats only — factory-primed steel/fiberglass (adequate factory primer) or field-primed

issues.description: Resolution proposed FAC_XDOR_COMPLEXITY grand_entry at 5.00; Estimation Engineer calibrated to 3.50 (within research range 3.00-5.00x). Acknowledged — Estimation Engineer has authority to calibrate within range.
Worst-case modifier stacking (~10.21x) vastly exceeds 4.0x cap. Grand_entry + QT5 flagged for hourly pricing review. 4.0x cap is deliberate safety mechanism.
Intercoat tasks use appears_in_tiers in SOP vs applies_when.quality_tier in production — different structural patterns, functionally equivalent.

doctrine_checks_passed: THREADING-1 through THREADING-6 (task ID completeness, classification match, applies_when consistency, UOM match, task prefix, module prefix)
EXT-1 through EXT-7 (key namespace, substrate state, protection zone, site conditions, factor keys, modifier math, material state)
DOOR-1 through DOOR-9 (EA rates, complexity primary driver, fiberglass acrylic-only, steel DTM, wood six-side seal, IR-reflective, hardware, glass masking, QT range)
COMPLETENESS-1 through COMPLETENESS-5 (protection zones, cross-spec boundaries, round configurations, module phase order, input declarations)

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup -> Prep -> Prime (bare substrates) -> Finish 1 -> Interstage -> Finish 2 -> Reinstall -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Walkway protection -> Hardware removal -> Weatherstrip protection -> Threshold protection -> Glass masking -> Equipment setup -> Coating work -> Hardware/weatherstrip reinstall -> Operation test -> Final inspect -> Touch-up -> Glass unmask -> Threshold teardown -> Walkway teardown -> Tool clean
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Prep (substrate-driven) -> Prime (1 coat, skipped for factory-primed/field-primed) -> Finish coat 1 -> Interstage (inspect, sand QT4/QT5, repair, dust) -> Finish coat 2 -> Final inspect -> Touch up
sequencing_notes.panel_door_sequence: Brush recesses first (panels, then stiles, then rails) -> Spray/brush faces -> Brush edges -> Mullions (grand_entry only)
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO roller application. NO back-rolling on metal doors. NO oil-based products on fiberglass. NO hydrocarbon solvents on fiberglass. NO sanding of textured (stain-grade) fiberglass.

relationships.notes: First exterior door spec. Adjacent to trim spec (casing). No direct siding adjacency (casing intervenes). Key departures from interior door spec: EA per assembly (not EA_SIDE), 3 substrate materials, DTM primer path, IR-reflective requirement, six-side sealing, hardware removal mandate.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior entry door prime and paint. First exterior door spec — EA-based single-item spec (ITM_DOOR_EXT) with 3 substrate materials (steel/fiberglass/wood), 3 complexity tiers (single_slab/panel/grand_entry), 3 sheens (satin/semi-gloss/gloss), 2 application methods (spray/brush), QT3-QT5 quality tiers (QT2 excluded). 46 tasks across 8 modules (24 binary, 18 qt_scaled, 4 qt_conditional). 6 material systems (3 primers + 2 finishes + 1 IR-reflective specialty). 5 protection zones. 8 factor modifiers. 2 round configurations (3-coat for bare substrates, 2-coat for factory/field-primed). Context prefix XDOR. Key features: hardware removal mandate, fiberglass 100% acrylic restriction, DTM primer for bare steel, wood six-side seal, IR-reflective HARD STOP for LRV < 30, door complexity as primary cost driver. QA result: pass (3 minor issues, 0 blockers).
